No unit suites were run this time, since no code changed.
discoveries: **A correction to my last return:** the code commit's 12-digit hash is **ee5056be590a**, not ee5056be1f6c. I had written the last four digits without reading them; `git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD` confirms ee5056be590a, which matches the lead's figure. Also: `_checked` runs twice per retrieval call, 672 times, for 10.4–16.3 s. §2 of the record based its estimate of that cost on one stat sweep per call. The measured time is inside that estimate, and §4 says so; I did not edit §2.
risks: Every wall time includes cProfile's overhead and the load was not controlled. Within pairs 2 and 3 the "after" run had the lighter load, so part of each wall-time saving is the load, not the change. The record says both.
lessons: Write a commit hash only after reading it from `git rev-parse --short=12`, never from the 8-digit `--oneline` output.
proposed_decisions: The verdict on option (b), for the owner (DEC-969), is: don't make batching the next step.
- At mean loads of about 10 and 20, the check already finishes under 600 s (300 s and 406 s), and embedding is 2 % and 8 % of the run.
- At a mean of 36 (940 s), removing all 373 s of embedding would still leave 567 s. Batching would have to cut it to under 33 s, and nothing in these figures shows that.
- At 40 or more, the figures say nothing.

My confidence is medium: high for loads up to 20, low above 36.
unresolved: KPI 4's run at a load of 40 or more is still owed. No mean reached 40; the highest was 36.2, with peaks of 46.8, and a 46-minute wait for 40 saw the load fall to 0.2. A further open point: at a mean of 36, 550 s of the run is outside the freshness checks and outside query embedding, and this measure does not break it down.
recommended_next_action: The lead or orchestrator decides whether the run at load 40 or more is repeated before close, or the gap is recorded, and brings the verdict on option (b) to the owner.
